title: Bones of the foot (dorsal)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

structures.name: Talus
objects: Talus.r

rows: Location
The tarsal bone that sits on the calcaneus and passes the weight of the body from the tibia to the foot.
Articulates with
Tibia and fibula at the ankle joint, the calcaneus below and the navicular in front.
Features
Head, neck and body. The trochlea on top of the body fits between the two malleoli. No muscle attaches to the talus.
hy: A fracture of the neck of the talus can cut off the blood supply to the body of the bone, which may then die (avascular necrosis).

structures.name: Calcaneus
objects: Calcaneus.r

rows: Location
The heel bone; the largest tarsal bone.
Articulates with
Talus above and the cuboid in front.
Features
Calcaneal tuberosity, where the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon inserts. Sustentaculum tali, a shelf on the medial side that supports the talus.
hy: The tarsal bone most often fractured, typically in a fall from a height onto the heels. A compression fracture of the lumbar spine may go with it, so the spine is checked as well.

structures.name: Navicular
objects: Navicular bone.r

rows: Location
Tarsal bone on the medial side of the foot, between the head of the talus and the three cuneiforms.
Articulates with
Talus behind and the three cuneiforms in front; sometimes the cuboid at its lateral side.
Features
Tuberosity on its medial side, the main insertion of tibialis posterior.

structures.name: Cuboid
objects: Cuboid bone.r

rows: Location
Tarsal bone on the lateral side of the foot, in front of the calcaneus.
Articulates with
Calcaneus behind, the fourth and fifth metatarsals in front, and the lateral cuneiform on its medial side; sometimes the navicular.
Features
Groove on its plantar surface for the tendon of fibularis longus.

structures.name: Medial cuneiform
objects: Medial cuneiform bone.r

rows: Location
The largest of the three cuneiforms, on the medial side of the foot in front of the navicular.
Articulates with
Navicular, the intermediate cuneiform, and the first and second metatarsals.
Features
Tibialis anterior and fibularis longus both insert on it and on the base of the first metatarsal.

structures.name: Intermediate cuneiform
objects: Intermediate cuneiform bone.r

rows: Location
The smallest cuneiform, between the medial and lateral cuneiforms.
Articulates with
Navicular, the medial and lateral cuneiforms, and the second metatarsal.
Features
It is shorter than its neighbors, so the base of the second metatarsal is set back between them.

structures.name: Lateral cuneiform
objects: Lateral cuneiform bone.r

rows: Location
Between the intermediate cuneiform and the cuboid.
Articulates with
Navicular, the intermediate cuneiform, the cuboid, and the second, third and fourth metatarsals.
Features
Wedge-shaped like the other cuneiforms, which helps form the transverse arch of the foot.

structures.name: 1st metatarsal
objects: First metatarsal bone.r

rows: Location
The bone of the foot behind the great toe; the shortest and thickest metatarsal.
Articulates with
Medial cuneiform at its base and the proximal phalanx of the great toe at its head.
Features
Two sesamoid bones lie under its head, in the tendons of flexor hallucis brevis.

structures.name: 2nd metatarsal
objects: Second metatarsal bone.r

rows: Location
The bone of the foot behind the second toe; the longest metatarsal.
Articulates with
All three cuneiforms and the third metatarsal at its base, and the proximal phalanx of the second toe at its head.
Features
Its base is wedged between the medial and lateral cuneiforms, which makes it the least mobile metatarsal.
hy: A common site of stress (march) fractures in runners and military recruits.

structures.name: 3rd metatarsal
objects: Third metatarsal bone.r

rows: Location
The bone of the foot behind the third toe.
Articulates with
Lateral cuneiform and the second and fourth metatarsals at its base, and the proximal phalanx of the third toe at its head.
Features
Base, shaft and head, like the other metatarsals.

structures.name: 4th metatarsal
objects: Fourth metatarsal bone.r

rows: Location
The bone of the foot behind the fourth toe.
Articulates with
Cuboid, the lateral cuneiform and the third and fifth metatarsals at its base, and the proximal phalanx of the fourth toe at its head.
Features
Base, shaft and head, like the other metatarsals.

structures.name: 5th metatarsal
objects: Fifth metatarsal bone.r

rows: Location
The bone on the lateral border of the foot, behind the little toe.
Articulates with
Cuboid and the fourth metatarsal at its base, and the proximal phalanx of the little toe at its head.
Features
A tuberosity projects from the lateral side of its base. Fibularis brevis inserts on it.
hy: In a forced inversion of the foot the pull of fibularis brevis can tear the tuberosity off the base (avulsion fracture). A fracture a little farther along, where the base meets the shaft (Jones fracture), heals poorly.

structures.name: Proximal phalanges of the toes
objects: Proximal phalanx of first finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of second finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of third finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of fourth finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r

rows: Location
The first bone of each toe, next to the metatarsal.
Features
Five in all. Each has a base that meets the head of its metatarsal, a shaft and a head.

structures.name: Middle phalanges of the toes
objects: Middle phalanx of second finger of foot.r
Middle phalanx of third finger of foot.r
Middle phalanx of fourth finger of foot.r
Middle phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r

rows: Location
The second bone of each of the four lateral toes. The great toe has no middle phalanx.
Features
Four in all, short and broad. In the little toe the middle phalanx is often fused with the distal one.

structures.name: Distal phalanges of the toes
objects: Distal phalanx of first finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of second finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of third finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of fourth finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r

rows: Location
The bone at the tip of each toe.
Features
Five in all. Each ends in a rough tuberosity that supports the pulp of the toe and the nail.
